existing_stems.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes abstraction from encapsulation?
existing_stems.ans_text: Abstraction presents a simplified interface and hides implementation detail, while encapsulation binds data together with the operations on it and controls access to them

existing_stems.ans_text: The base class destructor must be declared virtual

existing_stems.q: An extraction such as in >> x is attempted on a file stream when no data remains. Which stream state results, and why does the stream then test as false?
existing_stems.ans_text: eofbit and failbit are both set, and it is failbit that makes the stream test false

existing_stems.leaf: I/O streams and file handling in OOP
existing_stems.q: What is the difference between opening a file with ios::app and opening it with ios::ate?
existing_stems.ans_text: ios::app sends every write to the end of the file, whereas ios::ate only positions the pointer at the end when the file is opened

existing_stems.q: Why is an exception of class type normally caught by reference rather than by value?
existing_stems.ans_text: A by-value handler copies the thrown object and slices a derived exception down to the handler's base type

existing_stems.q: A try block lists a handler for catch (const std::exception&) before a handler for catch (const std::out_of_range&). What happens when an out_of_range object is thrown inside that try block?
existing_stems.ans_text: The std::exception handler runs, because handlers are examined in the order they are written

existing_stems.q: For a std::string holding 5 characters, how does at(9) differ in behaviour from operator[](9)?
existing_stems.ans_text: at(9) throws std::out_of_range, while operator[](9) is unchecked and gives undefined behaviour
